subject: [PATCH 1/2] btrfs: allocate additional SYSTEM space earlier

reviews.author: Filipe Manana
reviews.summary: Reviewer Filipe Manana questioned the logic of one specific hunk in the patch, pointing out that if left >= bytes is always true at this point because a system chunk has already been allocated when left < bytes.
reviews.raw_body:
So this hunk I have trouble understanding it, because if left >= bytes
should always be true at this point, as if if left < bytes we have
allocated a system chunk (if we haven't then ret has an error value).

Otherwise it looks good (as well as the second patch).

Thanks.

reviews.author: Boris Burkov (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged that the current condition in reserve_chunk_space() can be confusing and proposed to rename system_space_needed() to system_space_target() to better differentiate between the need for a new system chunk and the minimum space required for future allocations.
reviews.raw_body:
It is a bit confusing and I am not sure how to make it as nice as
possible. So the condition is:

  low = left < bytes || info->total_bytes < system_space_needed(info)
  ...
  if (low) {
  ...
  }

So ret != 0 implies low is true, but not necessarily left < bytes.
Basically the idea is that if the chunk allocation designed to protect
the chunk space in the future fails but we still have enough for right
now (ret && left >= bytes) then we can still add bytes to the block_rsv.

Would it help if I tried to give separate names to the two conditions
and did something like:

needs_space = left < bytes
wants_space = total < system_space_target()
low = needs_space || wants_space

...

if (!ret || !needs_space) {
 ...
}

So rename system_space_needed() to system_space_target() or something
like that, and then differentiate the minimum to add to the block_rsv
more clearly from the desire to add a system chunk? The current
system_space_needed() is kinda misleaded cause with writeback re-cowing,
we might use more than that in a txn anyway so it is not a hard
guarantee.

Thanks for the review,
Boris

2026-09-28.patch_summary: This patch addresses a performance issue in Btrfs file systems where large block devices can accumulate thousands of system chunks, leading to slow deletion of unused block groups when the file system is filled up and then freed en-masse. The problem arises because the current implementation allocates new system chunks only when the space left is smaller than the reservation for a single chunk tree update. To fix this, the patch introduces a new function `system_space_needed` that estimates the upper bound on bytes needed to modify every leaf in the chunk tree and allocates additional system space earlier, ensuring that all block groups can be deleted in one transaction.
